segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hello, I'm Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Welcome to Real Easy English from BBC Learning English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Every week we have a real conversation in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can find the vocabulary from this episode and a text version to read along on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: How are you, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm well, thank you, Georgie. How are you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm pretty good too, thank you. I'm very excited for the weekend.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh, really? Well, today we're talking all about the weekend.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We're going to talk about what we plan to do at the weekend.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Great, let's start.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, do you have any weekend plans?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I do have plans. I'm going to visit my parents at the weekend,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: so I'm going to get the train to my hometown. What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't really have any special plans but I might spend lots of time doing sport with

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: my kids.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Mm Nice Which sports

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Cricket in the summer and football as well

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Nice So that what you usually do

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That what I usually do I usually spend most of the weekend taking my kids to sport

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Do you like it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Actually, I really do. I really do like it. It's fun to watch them trying their hardest.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, nice. Is there anything else you'd like to do this weekend?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, I might meet up with a friend and we might go for some food or maybe just a drink or we might go for a walk or something.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Nice.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And how about you, Georgie? What do you plan to do when you get home?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, we have a lunch on Saturday and we live in the countryside, so we'll probably go for a walk with the dogs and we're likely to go to the pub as well.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Is this a typical weekend for you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's not because I don't usually go home to see my parents.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Most weekends I stay in London, I meet some friends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah so this is not a typical weekend but it nice to visit my parents

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What are you looking forward to

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: This weekend

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I really looking forward to spending time in the countryside When I in London I really miss the peace and quiet

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: and I miss my dog. So I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And it's good to get some fresh air.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, exactly. Exactly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Georgie, you said you are looking forward to being in the countryside.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I did.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And looking forward to means that you're excited about something you're going to do in the

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: future.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Exactly. Yes. Like I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Is your dog looking forward to

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: seeing you?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, I'm sure he is. So Neil, I have quite clear plans. I know what I'm going to do

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: this weekend. And to talk about plans like that, we usually use be going to or the present continuous.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I said, I'm going to visit my parents at the weekend.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And sometimes we shorten going to, to gonna when we're speaking quickly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Now your plans are certain, mine are not so certain.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I used might and may I said I might meet my friend I may go for a meal or I may go for a drink It means I not completely sure

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, Neil, I'm sure whatever you do this weekend, you'll have a nice time.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, let's look at the vocabulary we learned during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We learned might, which we use to talk about possible plans.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I might meet my friend.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Going to, which we use to talk about future plans

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: that are a little bit more certain.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And looking forward to, which means

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to be pleased or excited that something is going to happen.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But I'm looking forward to the next episode

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: when we'll talk about saving the planet.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you can't wait, you can find lots of courses, programmes and activities on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bye for now.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Goodbye.
